---
name: moe-gemm-screening
description: "How to screen a build of the LLM's grouped MoE GEMM (llm_moe_gemm.comp) from disk, and the two traps hit doing it on 2026-09-29."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: cd78a9a3-9df7-41bb-898c-6e666a202333
  modified: 2026-09-29T22:20:08.655Z
---

`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are
`moeSPIRV`'s keys in `llm/gpu_moe.go`; the auto plan is m2 at ≤1024 tokens and
m4 above, so a 2048-token screen must override `up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build
(WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one.

**Why:** two traps cost time on 2026-09-29 (KERNELS.md G5a, research/2.11).
The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. And a `-moe` arm
at 60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean.

**How to apply:** build arms with glslc to the scratchpad (the generate line's
flags from `shaders/shaders.go` plus the knob), `cmp` the knob-less build
against the shipped `.spv` (ids may differ; compare `cmd/probe` instruction
counts), gate with `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (maxAbs must be 0 against m2/m2),
then time. A control that removes work can read above the pipe's ceiling only
if the compiler dropped MMAs; check the `v_wmma` count in the disassembly
before trusting it. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and
[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].
---
name: llm-test-suite-gotchas
description: "Three ways go test ./llm/ misleads: Go's 10-minute default timeout, a TestGraphLogits failure that is pre-existing on main, and a relative LLM_BANK_CACHE writing 23 GB into llm/."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:36.040Z
---

**`go test ./llm/` needs `-timeout 60m`.** Go's default is ten minutes and the
suite runs past it inside `TestQSASelectionSurvivesOurScores`. What you get is
a panic stack and `FAIL strix-halo-vulkan/llm 600.024s`, which **reads as a
real failure and is not one**. With a warm bank cache the whole suite is
~180 s; cold it is much longer.

**`TestGraphLogits` passes as of 2026-09-22** — it now takes a near-tie on
argmax (7 tokens, "The capital of France is Paris."). Its diagnostics at
f062e28 are `result_output ... maxAbs 1.987e+00 at 19208, rms 3.314e-01`,
argmax ours 11751 vs llama.cpp 561, "0.4920 apart" — P16's three changes
reproduce them byte for byte. (The older `2.507e+00 at 141557` digits are from
before the test changed.) To get a base to diff against, a `git worktree` of
HEAD needs `models/` and `reference/out/` symlinked in (both gitignored) and
the `.spv` files copied, or the test silently prints nothing.

**That identity is also the cheapest whole-model bit-exactness check there
is.** A change that claims to be bit-exact should reproduce those numbers to
the digit through all 48 layers — stronger than any block test, and it costs
one 61 s run.

**`LLM_BANK_CACHE` is a relative path, and `go test ./llm/` resolves it
against `llm/`.** So exporting the usual
`LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache` and running the
tests silently builds a **23 GB** duplicate at `llm/models/`, untracked. Use
an absolute path, or `rm -rf llm/models` afterwards. The real cache
(26 GB, 199 files) is at the repo root.

**How to apply:** the useful per-change gates are
`go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttn|TestMoEGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit' -timeout 30m`
(~80 s), and run the full suite only when something broad moved. See
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
---
name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
description: "`go run` rebuilds per arm, and a rebuilt shared test binary is picked up by a still-running loop: build once per sweep under its own name, check ps before a second GPU run."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with

    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found

~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
until the end.

[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the

---
name: moe-gemm-screening
description: "How to screen a build of the LLM's grouped MoE GEMM (llm_moe_gemm.comp) from disk, and the two traps hit doing it on 2026-09-29."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project

  modified: 2026-09-29T22:20:08.655Z
---

`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are
`moeSPIRV`'s keys in `llm/gpu_moe.go`; the auto plan is m2 at ≤1024 tokens and
m4 above, so a 2048-token screen must override `up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build
(WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one.

**Why:** two traps cost time on 2026-09-29 (KERNELS.md G5a, research/2.11).
The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. And a `-moe` arm
at 60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean.

**How to apply:** build arms with glslc to the scratchpad (the generate line's
flags from `shaders/shaders.go` plus the knob), `cmp` the knob-less build
against the shipped `.spv` (ids may differ; compare `cmd/probe` instruction
counts), gate with `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (maxAbs must be 0 against m2/m2),
then time. A control that removes work can read above the pipe's ceiling only
if the compiler dropped MMAs; check the `v_wmma` count in the disassembly
before trusting it. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and
[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].
---
name: llm-test-suite-gotchas
description: "Three ways go test ./llm/ misleads: Go's 10-minute default timeout, a TestGraphLogits failure that is pre-existing on main, and a relative LLM_BANK_CACHE writing 23 GB into llm/."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:36.040Z
---

**`go test ./llm/` needs `-timeout 60m`.** Go's default is ten minutes and the
suite runs past it inside `TestQSASelectionSurvivesOurScores`. What you get is
a panic stack and `FAIL strix-halo-vulkan/llm 600.024s`, which **reads as a
real failure and is not one**. With a warm bank cache the whole suite is
~180 s; cold it is much longer.

**`TestGraphLogits` passes as of 2026-09-22** — it now takes a near-tie on
argmax (7 tokens, "The capital of France is Paris."). Its diagnostics at
f062e28 are `result_output ... maxAbs 1.987e+00 at 19208, rms 3.314e-01`,
argmax ours 11751 vs llama.cpp 561, "0.4920 apart" — P16's three changes
reproduce them byte for byte. (The older `2.507e+00 at 141557` digits are from
before the test changed.) To get a base to diff against, a `git worktree` of
HEAD needs `models/` and `reference/out/` symlinked in (both gitignored) and
the `.spv` files copied, or the test silently prints nothing.

**That identity is also the cheapest whole-model bit-exactness check there
is.** A change that claims to be bit-exact should reproduce those numbers to
the digit through all 48 layers — stronger than any block test, and it costs
one 61 s run.

**`LLM_BANK_CACHE` is a relative path, and `go test ./llm/` resolves it
against `llm/`.** So exporting the usual
`LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache` and running the
tests silently builds a **23 GB** duplicate at `llm/models/`, untracked. Use
an absolute path, or `rm -rf llm/models` afterwards. The real cache
(26 GB, 199 files) is at the repo root.

**How to apply:** the useful per-change gates are
`go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttn|TestMoEGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit' -timeout 30m`
(~80 s), and run the full suite only when something broad moved. See
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

## P11-4: three ways to spend the padding, and none of them pays

The schedule rounds every expert's row range up to the widest row block any
dispatch runs, so that a tile's rows are always that expert's and a
cooperative-matrix store — which covers sixteen rows and cannot be masked —
goes straight to global. At a 2048-token ubatch that executes **38 912 rows
for 20 480 real ones, 1.90x**; at 512 it is 2.33x. It reads like the biggest
waste in the block.

The constraint is the **fragment**, sixteen rows, not the row block, so all
three attempts pad to sixteen and differ only in how the GEMM is told:

| | tiles | rows | `moe.up` at 2048 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| as shipped, pad 64 | 608 | 38 912 | **11 936 µs** |
| a row count per record, bound in the unrolled loops | 608 | 24 304 | 13 662 |
| the same, with the gather's trip count left compile-time | 608 | 24 304 | 12 520 |
| three sub-lists, one dispatch a rung, no bounds at all | 608 | 25 184 | 12 532 |
| BM 128 (`w2m4`/`w4m2`), pad 128 | 477 | 61 056 | 13 509 |

**35% fewer rows is worth nothing, and paying anything for it loses.**

- **A bound inside the loops costs more than the rows.** At BM 64 the
  per-fragment branch sits inside the doubly-unrolled accumulator loops and
  the kernel goes to 256 VGPRs; making the gather's trip count dynamic on top
  of that is another 1.1 ms, because four `uvec4` loads stop being one clause.
- **Three dispatches cost what the rows saved.** One sub-list per rung — 64,
  32 and 16 — needs no guard anywhere and every kernel stays exactly the code
  it was. It came out 5% *slower* than one dispatch of 608 full tiles: the
  small lists do not fill the machine, and three grids have three ramps.
  (It also found a real bug on the way in, which is the one part worth
  keeping: the two modes **share one permutation** and may be cut to different
  row blocks, so a row range that depends on the pass's `bm` puts the up
  mode's expert 7 where the down mode does not look. `m1/m4` is a rung of the
  ladder and `TestMoEGPUDownNarrowed` caught it.)
- **A wider block trades the wrong way.** BM 128 cuts the tile count 608 → 477
  but takes the padding to 2.98x, and loses by 1.13x. The tile count does not
  fall as far as it looks like it should, because at 2048 tokens 399 experts
  are touched and **the floor is one tile an expert** however wide the block.

Fitting a per-tile and a per-row cost to the rung ladder at fixed rows (`m1`
24 961 µs at 2432 tiles, `m2` 17 457 at 1216, `m4` 11 936 at 608) puts ~9 µs
on a tile and ~0.17 µs on a row — so at BM 64 the **tiles are 45% of the
dispatch and the rows 55%** on paper, and in practice the rows behave as if
they were free. The reading that survives all four measurements: a tile's cost
is dominated by unpacking a `BN x BK` slab of a 4.5-bit bank per K-step, that
work is the same whether the tile holds 16 rows or 64, and the matrix cores
absorb the rows it is multiplied into.

**So the way to make this kernel faster is fewer tiles at the same block
width** — which means fewer *experts touched*, which means a bigger ubatch.
Which is P11-1, and is why P11-1 is the whole of the result.

## P11-5: long context, and it is all one kernel

`cmd/llm -depth -pp 2048`, 48 layers, shipped banks, `wiki.test.raw`, one
sequence walked forward (`results/p11_depth.csv`):

| depth | pp tok/s | vs 0 | ms a token | hc | dn | moe | **attn** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | **1146.6** | 1.00x | 0.872 | 0.121 | 0.156 | 0.478 | 0.083 |

---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].

<!-- §2.10 — KERNELS.md G-o8. The section number is the stable identifier
     cited from shaders/, bench/, cmd/, vk/ and the root docs. Do not
     renumber it. -->

[← IDEAS.md](ideas.md) · [research index](README.md) · the LDS-staged GEMM's remaining points

### 2.10 Every VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe a clock: the LDS-staged GEMM's second K tile as a loop — **done** ✅ (2026-09-29)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G-o8, after §2.9): the shipped LDS-staged wave32
GEMM (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`) runs at 80% of the ceiling at its
clock, and with the staging loads all L0 hits at 82%, so the ~18 points
left are on the LDS side of the kernel: 64 `ds_load_b64`, 6 stores, a
barrier and a `lgkmcnt` ladder a slab. Which of those is it?

**Answer: mostly none of them.** The largest single cost was ~40
`v_swap_b32`/`v_mov_b32` a K tile that the register allocator emits to
assemble the slab's *second* tile's fragments, because the scheduler had
hoisted the next slab's six staging loads above this slab's MMAs and the
second tile's `ds_load`s then landed in whatever pairs were free. On this
part **a VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe about one clock** (the
WMMA runs on the SIMD's VALU; there is no separate tensor unit to
overlap with), so those moves were ~7% of the pipe. Keeping the slab's
two K tiles as a loop the compiler may not unroll (`KT_LOOP`), with the
staging views declared writable so NIR does not sink the staging loads to
their use (`STAGE_RW`), takes the moves out: **same MMAs in the same
order, bit-identical**, H3's projections **40.4 → 43.5 TFLOP/s**, the
split down projection 40.3 → 42.2, a 480p forward **27.30 → 26.71 s**,
**80 → 85% per clock**. Shipped as the same build name, so all nine
hosts of the kernel (§2.9's G8 table) get it with no host change.

**The instrument: a probe that adds the kernel's parts back one at a
time.** `shaders/wmma_issue_probe.comp` is the register-only WMMA loop of
`alu_peak.comp` in the GEMM's own geometry (eight wave32 waves of 4×4
tiles, 55 KB of LDS planes at pitch 36), run through `cmd/bench peak` by
the new `PEAK_SPV` hook (`bench/ops_peak.go`), against the same 480
FLOP/clk/CU:

| added to the register-only loop | FLOP/clk/CU | of 480 |
|---|---|---|
| nothing (`wmma_issue_reg`) | 480–491 | 100% |
| 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 independent fp32 FMAs a lane per MMA | 449 / 422 / 382 / 318 | 93.5 / 88 / 80 / 66% |
| a workgroup barrier every 16 MMAs | 480 | 100% |
| the A fragments re-read from LDS each tile (4 a 16 MMAs) | 475 | 99% |
| A and B re-read from LDS (the GEMM's 8 a 16 MMAs, 32 `ds_load_b64`) | 467 | 97% |
| the LDS reads **and** the barrier | 438 | 91% |
| the reads as 16-lane exchanges (`XCHG`: half the LDS bytes, +12 VALU a fragment) | 397 | 83% |
| the exchange and the barrier | 384 | 80% |

Four things it settles. **VALU issue is not free beside the MMAs**: four
FMAs per MMA cost 12%, which is 4 clocks of a 34-clock wave32 MMA, and it
stays linear to 8 a MMA (dual-issue softens 16). So the 16-MMA tile's
budget for everything that is not an MMA is a few instructions, and the
shipped kernel was spending ~50. **The LDS bandwidth is not the limit**:
the GEMM's own read pattern costs 3% (G-o8's "LDS rate for replicated
reads" candidate is dead), and a barrier alone costs nothing. **The two
together cost 9%**: the burst of every wave's reads after the barrier,
which is the lockstep candidate, and which is confirmed on the real kernel
below. And **halving the LDS bytes with `v_permlanex16` loses**: the
exchange is 4 permutes and 8 selects a fragment (ACO lowers
`subgroupShuffleXor(v, 16)` at wave32 to `v_permlanex16_b32`, a VALU op

### 2.10 Every VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe a clock: the LDS-staged GEMM's second K tile as a loop — **done** ✅ (2026-09-29)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G-o8, after §2.9): the shipped LDS-staged wave32
GEMM (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`) runs at 80% of the ceiling at its
clock, and with the staging loads all L0 hits at 82%, so the ~18 points
left are on the LDS side of the kernel: 64 `ds_load_b64`, 6 stores, a
barrier and a `lgkmcnt` ladder a slab. Which of those is it?

**Answer: mostly none of them.** The largest single cost was ~40
`v_swap_b32`/`v_mov_b32` a K tile that the register allocator emits to
assemble the slab's *second* tile's fragments, because the scheduler had
hoisted the next slab's six staging loads above this slab's MMAs and the
second tile's `ds_load`s then landed in whatever pairs were free. On this
part **a VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe about one clock** (the
WMMA runs on the SIMD's VALU; there is no separate tensor unit to
overlap with), so those moves were ~7% of the pipe. Keeping the slab's
two K tiles as a loop the compiler may not unroll (`KT_LOOP`), with the
staging views declared writable so NIR does not sink the staging loads to
their use (`STAGE_RW`), takes the moves out: **same MMAs in the same
order, bit-identical**, H3's projections **40.4 → 43.5 TFLOP/s**, the
split down projection 40.3 → 42.2, a 480p forward **27.30 → 26.71 s**,
**80 → 85% per clock**. Shipped as the same build name, so all nine
hosts of the kernel (§2.9's G8 table) get it with no host change.

**The instrument: a probe that adds the kernel's parts back one at a
time.** `shaders/wmma_issue_probe.comp` is the register-only WMMA loop of
`alu_peak.comp` in the GEMM's own geometry (eight wave32 waves of 4×4
tiles, 55 KB of LDS planes at pitch 36), run through `cmd/bench peak` by
the new `PEAK_SPV` hook (`bench/ops_peak.go`), against the same 480
FLOP/clk/CU:

| added to the register-only loop | FLOP/clk/CU | of 480 |
|---|---|---|
| nothing (`wmma_issue_reg`) | 480–491 | 100% |
| 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 independent fp32 FMAs a lane per MMA | 449 / 422 / 382 / 318 | 93.5 / 88 / 80 / 66% |
| a workgroup barrier every 16 MMAs | 480 | 100% |
| the A fragments re-read from LDS each tile (4 a 16 MMAs) | 475 | 99% |
| A and B re-read from LDS (the GEMM's 8 a 16 MMAs, 32 `ds_load_b64`) | 467 | 97% |
| the LDS reads **and** the barrier | 438 | 91% |
| the reads as 16-lane exchanges (`XCHG`: half the LDS bytes, +12 VALU a fragment) | 397 | 83% |

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

lines: +// **Every single-wave build is a `SHORT` build** (KERNELS.md G5c, §2.12):
+// the permutation aligns experts to one fragment instead of the block, and
+// the kernel runs one of WM copies of its loop on the record's real rows.
+// The Q4_K up m4 build keeps only its 2- and 4-tile copies
+// (`SHORT_MIN=2`): a third copy spills 15 registers there, and a 16-row
+// tile costs it what a 32-row one does. The multi-wave rungs keep whole
+// blocks, and the host aligns to them when a plan names one.
// The Q4_K up builds carry `-DPIPE=2` (KERNELS.md G5, §2.11): the K loop as
// a software pipeline, the next step's bank and activation bytes fetched into

---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

research/README.md:65:| [§2.2](2.2-q4-coopmat.md) | Q4 into the coopmat path | **2.10x a MoE block**; LDS round-trip is unavoidable |
research/README.md:68:| [§2.11](2.11-moe-gemm-pipeline.md) | The grouped MoE GEMM's K loop as a software pipeline | **The up projection 1.68x at 2048 tokens (2.01x at 512, 1.57x at 4096), bit-identical; 22 → 37 TFLOP/s executed.** The controls say the LDS round trip §2.2 blamed is ~8 points and the loop without its stagings runs at the pipe; the cost was the dependent, divergent bank-load chain in front of every K-step, each block's lines re-read two to eight times. Fetch a step ahead, a header once a super-block, a nibble group once per two steps; the register-built fragment (G5 as written) has nothing to buy |
research/README.md:69:| [§2.10](2.10-valu-costs-matrix-clocks.md) | Every VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe a clock; the LDS-staged GEMM's second K tile as a loop | **80 → 85% per clock, bit-identical; H3's projections 40.4 → 43.5 TFLOP/s, a 480p forward 27.3 → 26.7 s.** The register allocator's ~40 `v_swap`/`v_mov` a tile were 7% of the pipe; a probe that adds the kernel's parts back to the register-only loop prices VALU at ~3% an instruction a MMA, the LDS reads at 3%, the barrier's lockstep at 6–9, and the 16-lane exchange (`v_permlanex16`) as a loss |
research/README.md:118:| [P12](p12-prefill-round-two.md) | **Prefill round two: two bit-exact kernel changes, and four of P11's own leads measured away.** Prefill is **1.012-1.025x on both axes** — 1191.2 → **1207.7 tok/s** at 2048 rows, 1370.5 → **1403.9** at 8192 (**3.59x** llama.cpp), and 651.3 → **667.7** at 64 000 cells — with the two base passes agreeing to 1370.5/1370.5 and 651.3/651.2. Two changes hold. **The attention kernel's row max ran on sixteen lanes of sixty-four**: `for (i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE)` with BM 16 and WAVE 64, KTIL times a block, two barriers and a store around each pass, each active lane then walking TILE cells serially with a `selected()` bit test. The whole key block is now staged at once (`stage` holds QT\*KTIL tiles, 2 KB of LDS) and RCL = WAVE/BM lanes share a row, folded by a **clustered subgroup max** — **bit-identical**, because a max has no rounding and the cells scanned are the same ones in the same order, and the wave is converged where the op is issued. **1.16x on the kernel at 512 tokens** and **+1.6-1.8% of a prefill token from 8000 cells on**. And **a K-quant block's header is one sixteen-byte load, not four dwords**: Q4_K/Q5_K open every block with `d`, `dmin` and twelve packed scale bytes, so at BK 32 a lane was issuing eight scalar loads a K-step against the nibbles' four `uvec4`s — L5b-7's rule for the third time. Every block of both formats is 16-byte aligned (region, row and block all multiples of 16) and `MoEGPU.build` now says so rather than trusting it; with the nibble extracted in two ops instead of four it is **`moe.up` 12 118 → 11 755 µs at 2048 tokens (1.031x)** with **`moe.down` (IQ4_NL, untouched) flat as the control**. **And four refusals, which close most of P11's open list.** **Both of `hc.cn`'s named suspects cost nothing**: deleting the 256-way reduction tree outright measures **5331.5 µs against 5325.8** — the eight barriers four times a token are **free**, so the non-bit-exact rewrite queued behind them would have bought zero — and replacing the per-token `gamma` read with a constant measures **5332.9**, because it is the same 40 KB every token and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy bandwidth is now unexplained *and* out of hypotheses. **The block skip hoisted out of the loop is 1.00x at every depth**: at 64k a query tile walks ~2000 blocks and skips ~1480, each paying a **dependent** global read, and a cost model where a dead block is ~20% of a live one reproduces `attn.attn`'s 9.8-against-16.0 TFLOP/s exactly — so the whole key range was voted on up front in one coalesced pass with a subgroup ballot, no atomics and no per-block barrier, and it bought **nothing**. The reason is the **exact converse of P8**: a decode step dispatches 24 single-wave workgroups and nothing hides a serial walk, but a 2048-token prefill dispatches **3072**, so that latency is already covered — *latency that matters at decode does not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy*. It is still live for decode, where it was deliberately never built. **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%**, not the rest of the gap. **The MoE's per-element affine is a floor**: gutting the whole scale path is 1.21x at 2048 tokens, P12-2 takes the loads and integer ops out of that, and what remains — an int→float convert, an FMA and an f16 convert on every weight — has no bit-exact cheaper form, since packed fp16 costs thirteen bits of mantissa and `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds the wrong way. **The ubatch remains the largest number on the board**: 2048 → 8192 is 1.16x and the curve has not flattened, which is a memory budget rather than a kernel. |
research/README.md:129:| [P1](p1-decode-attribution.md) | **The decode step, attributed to the dispatch: LLM2's "~12 ms unexplained" is 5.54 ms of weight-streaming dispatches below 227 GB/s, 3.46 ms of dispatches that stream no weight, and 3.01 ms of host.** The step sums to 30.52 ms with a 5 us residual over 36 dispatch labels and six host phases. **The n-gram gather was disk latency, and it was serial**: sixteen random rows of a 28.80 GB mmap'd table are **16.3 major faults a step**, served one at a time — issuing them concurrently leaves the fault count identical to two decimal places and is **7.0-7.5x** (853/819 us → 122/109), taking the gather 2.244 → 0.902 ms and decode **31.51 → 32.72 tok/s, 1.30x llama.cpp**. That is the other half of D9: `MADV_RANDOM` made each fault small, this stops them being serialised. Seven of eight weight-reading families measure 147-204 GB/s and **`hyper_conn` measures 114.6** — not bandwidth, since D14 says those weights never leave the MALL, but **485 dispatches a pass at 1.4-17 us each**: the block is 13.6% of the step for 8.4% of the bytes. `moe.down` is **147.5 GB/s against `moe.up`'s 200.6** off the same bank, a shape never re-screened (D11/D12). Idea 2's pre-recorded command buffer finally has a price — **1.96 ms, 6.4%, ~+2.2 tok/s** — and is the *fourth* item, not the first. **Idea 9 closed**: the 0.38 GB is the MoE router and the shared expert, which the inventory files as dense and the graph's table files with the MoE; every ceiling is now quoted on one basis, **4.281 GB a token** |
research/README.md:131:| [P3](p3-widths.md) | **L8c's knapsack, solved by measuring six complete plans instead of composing per-family deltas — and the answer is the small one. D18: the uniform 4.5-bit plan with `ple_proj` back on int8, 0.0165 GB a token for 0.367 points (4.1850, +3.87%, against the uniform plan's 4.2010, +4.27%), with the bank equal to the simulation to four decimals and the same standard error.** The decode cost is **below the instrument's floor**: three interleaved A/B pairs give means 35.74 against 35.79 with the sign flipping pair to pair, against a within-arm spread of 0.31 tok/s where the bytes predict 0.12 — one pair alone would have read −0.06, another +0.14. **The decision turned out to be three-way per family, not two**: `bank_q4.go:144` is nibbles by construction, so `q5_k` is a kernel stage (a third `qh` stream through the unpack) while int8 is free (a family left off the plan stages on L8a's bank). **The fifth bit recovers 66-77% of a family's whole 4.5-bit cost for a quarter of int8's bytes** — `full_attn` **4.1560 (+3.15%), 14.1 pp/GB**, `lm_head` 4.1743 at 8.0 (and it recovers 77% because unsloth's matrix has **no row for `output.weight`**, so the family is round-to-nearest), `ple_proj` 4.1919 at 47.8 for a 0.196 pp prize — where the *marginal* step from `q5_k` to int8 on `full_attn` is **1.9 pp/GB**, the clearest "stop here" on the frontier. **Idea 4 is closed with both its options losing**: `full_attn` at int8 measures **+2.72%** against the +2.07% additivity predicted, and is strictly dominated by L8c-3's `hc + attn` at `q5_k` (+2.70% at 4.419 GB against +2.72% at 4.592). **Additivity leaks both ways and both leaks are the n-gram block** — `ple_proj` marginal is 0.367 pp where standalone it is 0.59 (P2's 0.22 pp, from the other side), and `hc + attn` recovers 1.54 where the parts give ~1.39 — so **a plan is measured, never composed**. LLM2's ~12 pp/GB for `ple_proj` was quoted *from halves* where every other family was quoted from int8; on the consistent basis it is ~35. **A second corpus (Go stdlib, 145 chunks) leaves the ranking invariant at 2.5x smaller magnitudes** (1.6288 → 1.6560 uniform → 1.6506 D18 → 1.6450 `full_attn` q5_k), with `ple_proj` a *larger* share of the damage on code (20% against 8.7%) and the fifth bit recovering 41% against 26% — so **+3.87% is a wikitext figure and the pessimistic end**. Fresh inventory **4.281 GB a token, 56.5 tok/s ceiling** (arithmetic — not P1's identically-numbered *measured* 4.281). `cmd/serve -llm` stages D18 by default; `cmd/llm` deliberately does not |
research/README.md:132:| [P2](p2-ple-proj.md) | **The last streamed dense family on the 4.5-bit bank, the fp16 tail deleted from three kernels and three blocks, and L8c closed: the complete uniform plan as built is 4.2010 (+4.27%) over 145 chunks, beside the 4.1998 (+4.24%) L8c-3's simulation projected before any kernel existed — an identity after the deletion, because the bank now quantises exactly the set of weights the simulation always did (complete-plan bank ≡ full-scope sim, chunk for chunk, no `SRC=q8`).** `ple_proj` is two bank stages in one (65.8 MB of halves → 35.1 int8, bit-identical → **18.7 at 4.5 bits**), costs no new kernel — MODE 2 of `llm_gemm.comp` exists for this block — and is **the plan's worst trade**: +0.59% alone for 0.047 GB a token (~12 pp/GB, a family present at one layer run once), with an 8-chunk screen of −0.11%, the fifth screen failure and second sign flip. **Additivity breaks at the sixth family**: separate deltas sum to 4.31% where the plan measures 4.09% (tails fp16), the first 0.22 pp deviation where four families summed to 0.01. The deletion (D13's payoff) put alpha, beta, `inject` and the indexer on the plane at family width — **+0.18 pp measured**, ~0.085 GB a token back — after which the int8 bank is no longer bit-identical arithmetic on those four tensors: the trace tests carry that as `bankTol` at D13's measured prices and `TestGraphLogits` accepts an argmax flip only on a measured near-tie. Decode the same hour 28.400 → 28.336 → **27.865 ms, 35.89 tok/s, 1.43x llama.cpp**, on ~4.15 GB a token by subtraction |
research/README.md:153:| [L6a](l6a-residency.md) | **The whole model on the device at once — 84.20 GB of weights and 0.87 GB of arenas in 68 buffers, staged in 33 seconds, with 41 GB of the machine left over.** Every block in this vertical lays its weights out as one arena with a per-layer offset, and `maxStorageBufferRange` here is **4 GiB - 4** against an expert bank of 1.61 GB a layer — so residency was a question about the layout rather than a loop over the staging code. Binding 5 became an **array of buffers, one a layer**: a per-binding `descriptorCount` in the shim, a block-instance array in the GLSL indexed by a dynamically uniform push constant (core Vulkan, no descriptor indexing), NBANK compiled in at 48 with short stages padding the array, and the layer index riding in the **top sixteen bits of `moeUsed`** because the push block was already 64 uints against this device's 256-byte limit. The index is shown to be load-bearing rather than assumed: layer 3 read from bank 3 is 8.133e-05 rms against llama.cpp, and the same run with the index forced to zero is **203x further away** on a tensor of exactly the right shape and magnitude. **Residency is free in the bank's size** — 2, 4, 12, 24 and 48 banks are 10.4 to 84.2 GB resident and 11062-11242 us for the same block, a 1.6% spread with no trend, which is L0a's "the bus does not care how big the bank is" holding at 68 live buffers and the size the model actually is. What is left is a flat **~2.5%** step against L5b's isolated figure that appears with the other four blocks staged and does not grow with the bank, written down rather than chased. Three numbers that set up L6b: **68 buffers** against the "~100" estimate; **84.20 GB against the checkpoint's 82.52 GB core**, 1.04x once the un-staged embedding and lm head come off, the +3.04 GB being the dense half staged as **halves** (6.79 GB of fp16 against 3.67 of Q8_0, 1.85x); and the DeltaNet bank as the near miss at **4.18 GB in one buffer**, 2.7% under the cap. Staging order is worth 8 GB: the dense blocks first with their host floats dropped between them, because 36 DeltaNet layers dequantise to 8.35 GB of transient f32 at once |
research/README.md:165:| [L2a](l2a-prefill-attribution.md) | **Where llama.cpp's 393 tok/s prefill actually goes**, per op, from `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER` — and it settles L1's 5x. **The architecture is innocent**: `GATED_DELTA_NET` is **1.6%** of a prefill graph, the whole DeltaNet core 2.7%, full attention plus the QSA indexer 1.5%. Nor is it host overhead — **93% of the wall clock is GPU kernel time**. It is MoE experts 35.7%, dense matmul 26.2%, **elementwise glue 30.6%** and **tiny-N F32 matmul 12.2%**, of which `hc_*_inject` — a `[10240, 4]` F32 projection run 95 times a graph — is **10.3% of prefill at 31.8 GFLOP/s** and fuses into `hc.down` for free. Against this repo's own measured kernels the chunk is **2.25x on matmul** and **2.53x on the experts** (§2.2's Q4 grouped block), so **~1150 tok/s, not ~2000, is what L6 should be scoped against**. Two more: **`-ub 512` is a MALL-sized optimum** — 256/512/1024/2048 give 347.7/**391.4**/380.9/336.7, because the 10240-wide F32 residual is 20.97 MB at T=512 and 83.9 MB at T=2048, and the glue costs 1.57x more per token when it stops fitting; and at **decode** the matmuls are already at 198-230 GB/s, so the whole 25.15 -> 38.2 gap is **2896 weightless dispatches costing 8.9 ms, 22% of the step** — an order of magnitude past L1's 0.62 ms estimate |

# research/ — the findings archive

One file per **completed** experiment, plus (since the 2026-09-20
consolidation) the frozen per-vertical progress files. The live state of
play and the open items are in [`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md); this directory
is where a finished item's full write-up lives once it is closed, so an
agent can load one finding without loading all of them. The phase-1
backlog and the measured roofline are archived in [`ideas.md`](ideas.md).

## The vertical archives

The root progress files were consolidated here on 2026-09-20, frozen as
each vertical's closing record; stage letters (L7d, P4c, T9, S10, I7, E7…)
resolve inside them.

**`IMAGE.md` named two different files**, so a citation of it needs one
extra step: with a **Q-stage, a numbered decision or a Q-o number** it is
[`qimage-vertical.md`](qimage-vertical.md) (Qwen-Image-2.1, the root file
from 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-21); with an **I-stage (I0–I7)** it is

before that). Both spellings are live in code comments, which were not
rewritten — same as `LLM.md` and `SPEECH.md`.

And **a K-quant block's header is one sixteen-byte load, not four dwords**: Q4_K/Q5_K open every block with `d`, `dmin` and twelve packed scale bytes, so at BK 32 a lane was issuing eight scalar loads a K-step against the nibbles' four `uvec4`s — L5b-7's rule for the third time. Every block of both formats is 16-byte aligned (region, row and block all multiples of 16) and `MoEGPU.build` now says so rather than trusting it; with the nibble extracted in two ops instead of four it is **`moe.up` 12 118 → 11 755 µs at 2048 tokens (1.031x)** with **`moe.down` (IQ4_NL, untouched) flat as the control**. **And four refusals, which close most of P11's open list.** **Both of `hc.cn`'s named suspects cost nothing**: deleting the 256-way reduction tree outright measures **5331.5 µs against 5325.8** — the eight barriers four times a token are **free**, so the non-bit-exact rewrite queued behind them would have bought zero — and replacing the per-token `gamma` read with a constant measures **5332.9**, because it is the same 40 KB every token and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy bandwidth is now unexplained *and* out of hypotheses. **The block skip hoisted out of the loop is 1.00x at every depth**: at 64k a query tile walks ~2000 blocks and skips ~1480, each paying a **dependent** global read, and a cost model where a dead block is ~20% of a live one reproduces `attn.attn`'s 9.8-against-16.0 TFLOP/s exactly — so the whole key range was voted on up front in one coalesced pass with a subgroup ballot, no atomics and no per-block barrier, and it bought **nothing**. The reason is the **exact converse of P8**: a decode step dispatches 24 single-wave workgroups and nothing hides a serial walk, but a 2048-token prefill dispatches **3072**, so that latency is already covered — *latency that matters at decode does not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy*. It is still live for decode, where it was deliberately never built. **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%**, not the rest of the gap. **The MoE's per-element affine is a floor**: gutting the whole scale path is 1.21x at 2048 tokens, P12-2 takes the loads and integer ops out of that, and what remains — an int→float convert, an FMA and an f16 convert on every weight — has no bit-exact cheaper form, since packed fp16 costs thirteen bits of mantissa and `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds the wrong way. **The ubatch remains the largest number on the board**: 2048 → 8192 is 1.16x and the curve has not flattened, which is a memory budget rather than a kernel. |
research/README.md:129:| [P1](p1-decode-attribution.md) | **The decode step, attributed to the dispatch: LLM2's "~12 ms unexplained" is 5.54 ms of weight-streaming dispatches below 227 GB/s, 3.46 ms of dispatches that stream no weight, and 3.01 ms of host.** The step sums to 30.52 ms with a 5 us residual over 36 dispatch labels and six host phases. **The n-gram gather was disk latency, and it was serial**: sixteen random rows of a 28.80 GB mmap'd table are **16.3 major faults a step**, served one at a time — issuing them concurrently leaves the fault count identical to two decimal places and is **7.0-7.5x** (853/819 us → 122/109), taking the gather 2.244 → 0.902 ms and decode **31.51 → 32.72 tok/s, 1.30x llama.cpp**. That is the other half of D9: `MADV_RANDOM` made each fault small, this stops them being serialised. Seven of eight weight-reading families measure 147-204 GB/s and **`hyper_conn` measures 114.6** — not bandwidth, since D14 says those weights never leave the MALL, but **485 dispatches a pass at 1.4-17 us each**: the block is 13.6% of the step for 8.4% of the bytes. `moe.down` is **147.5 GB/s against `moe.up`'s 200.6** off the same bank, a shape never re-screened (D11/D12). Idea 2's pre-recorded command buffer finally has a price — **1.96 ms, 6.4%, ~+2.2 tok/s** — and is the *fourth* item, not the first. **Idea 9 closed**: the 0.38 GB is the MoE router and the shared expert, which the inventory files as dense and the graph's table files with the MoE; every ceiling is now quoted on one basis, **4.281 GB a token** |
research/README.md:131:| [P3](p3-widths.md) | **L8c's knapsack, solved by measuring six complete plans instead of composing per-family deltas — and the answer is the small one. D18: the uniform 4.5-bit plan with `ple_proj` back on int8, 0.0165 GB a token for 0.367 points (4.1850, +3.87%, against the uniform plan's 4.2010, +4.27%), with the bank equal to the simulation to four decimals and the same standard error.** The decode cost is **below the instrument's floor**: three interleaved A/B pairs give means 35.74 against 35.79 with the sign flipping pair to pair, against a within-arm spread of 0.31 tok/s where the bytes predict 0.12 — one pair alone would have read −0.06, another +0.14. **The decision turned out to be three-way per family, not two**: `bank_q4.go:144` is nibbles by construction, so `q5_k` is a kernel stage (a third `qh` stream through the unpack) while int8 is free (a family left off the plan stages on L8a's bank). **The fifth bit recovers 66-77% of a family's whole 4.5-bit cost for a quarter of int8's bytes** — `full_attn` **4.1560 (+3.15%), 14.1 pp/GB**, `lm_head` 4.1743 at 8.0 (and it recovers 77% because unsloth's matrix has **no row for `output.weight`**, so the family is round-to-nearest), `ple_proj` 4.1919 at 47.8 for a 0.196 pp prize — where the *marginal* step from `q5_k` to int8 on `full_attn` is **1.9 pp/GB**, the clearest "stop here" on the frontier. **Idea 4 is closed with both its options losing**: `full_attn` at int8 measures **+2.72%** against the +2.07% additivity predicted, and is strictly dominated by L8c-3's `hc + attn` at `q5_k` (+2.70% at 4.419 GB against +2.72% at 4.592). **Additivity leaks both ways and both leaks are the n-gram block** — `ple_proj` marginal is 0.367 pp where standalone it is 0.59 (P2's 0.22 pp, from the other side), and `hc + attn` recovers 1.54 where the parts give ~1.39 — so **a plan is measured, never composed**. LLM2's ~12 pp/GB for `ple_proj` was quoted *from halves* where every other family was quoted from int8; on the consistent basis it is ~35. **A second corpus (Go stdlib, 145 chunks) leaves the ranking invariant at 2.5x smaller magnitudes** (1.6288 → 1.6560 uniform → 1.6506 D18 → 1.6450 `full_attn` q5_k), with `ple_proj` a *larger* share of the damage on code (20% against 8.7%) and the fifth bit recovering 41% against 26% — so **+3.87% is a wikitext figure and the pessimistic end**. Fresh inventory **4.281 GB a token, 56.5 tok/s ceiling** (arithmetic — not P1's identically-numbered *measured* 4.281). `cmd/serve -llm` stages D18 by default; `cmd/llm` deliberately does not |
research/README.md:132:| [P2](p2-ple-proj.md) | **The last streamed dense family on the 4.5-bit bank, the fp16 tail deleted from three kernels and three blocks, and L8c closed: the complete uniform plan as built is 4.2010 (+4.27%) over 145 chunks, beside the 4.1998 (+4.24%) L8c-3's simulation projected before any kernel existed — an identity after the deletion, because the bank now quantises exactly the set of weights the simulation always did (complete-plan bank ≡ full-scope sim, chunk for chunk, no `SRC=q8`).** `ple_proj` is two bank stages in one (65.8 MB of halves → 35.1 int8, bit-identical → **18.7 at 4.5 bits**), costs no new kernel — MODE 2 of `llm_gemm.comp` exists for this block — and is **the plan's worst trade**: +0.59% alone for 0.047 GB a token (~12 pp/GB, a family present at one layer run once), with an 8-chunk screen of −0.11%, the fifth screen failure and second sign flip. **Additivity breaks at the sixth family**: separate deltas sum to 4.31% where the plan measures 4.09% (tails fp16), the first 0.22 pp deviation where four families summed to 0.01. The deletion (D13's payoff) put alpha, beta, `inject` and the indexer on the plane at family width — **+0.18 pp measured**, ~0.085 GB a token back — after which the int8 bank is no longer bit-identical arithmetic on those four tensors: the trace tests carry that as `bankTol` at D13's measured prices and `TestGraphLogits` accepts an argmax flip only on a measured near-tie. Decode the same hour 28.400 → 28.336 → **27.865 ms, 35.89 tok/s, 1.43x llama.cpp**, on ~4.15 GB a token by subtraction |
research/README.md:153:| [L6a](l6a-residency.md) | **The whole model on the device at once — 84.20 GB of weights and 0.87 GB of arenas in 68 buffers, staged in 33 seconds, with 41 GB of the machine left over.** Every block in this vertical lays its weights out as one arena with a per-layer offset, and `maxStorageBufferRange` here is **4 GiB - 4** against an expert bank of 1.61 GB a layer — so residency was a question about the layout rather than a loop over the staging code. Binding 5 became an **array of buffers, one a layer**: a per-binding `descriptorCount` in the shim, a block-instance array in the GLSL indexed by a dynamically uniform push constant (core Vulkan, no descriptor indexing), NBANK compiled in at 48 with short stages padding the array, and the layer index riding in the **top sixteen bits of `moeUsed`** because the push block was already 64 uints against this device's 256-byte limit. The index is shown to be load-bearing rather than assumed: layer 3 read from bank 3 is 8.133e-05 rms against llama.cpp, and the same run with the index forced to zero is **203x further away** on a tensor of exactly the right shape and magnitude. **Residency is free in the bank's size** — 2, 4, 12, 24 and 48 banks are 10.4 to 84.2 GB resident and 11062-11242 us for the same block, a 1.6% spread with no trend, which is L0a's "the bus does not care how big the bank is" holding at 68 live buffers and the size the model actually is. What is left is a flat **~2.5%** step against L5b's isolated figure that appears with the other four blocks staged and does not grow with the bank, written down rather than chased. Three numbers that set up L6b: **68 buffers** against the "~100" estimate; **84.20 GB against the checkpoint's 82.52 GB core**, 1.04x once the un-staged embedding and lm head come off, the +3.04 GB being the dense half staged as **halves** (6.79 GB of fp16 against 3.67 of Q8_0, 1.85x); and the DeltaNet bank as the near miss at **4.18 GB in one buffer**, 2.7% under the cap. Staging order is worth 8 GB: the dense blocks first with their host floats dropped between them, because 36 DeltaNet layers dequantise to 8.35 GB of transient f32 at once |
research/README.md:165:| [L2a](l2a-prefill-attribution.md) | **Where llama.cpp's 393 tok/s prefill actually goes**, per op, from `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER` — and it settles L1's 5x. **The architecture is innocent**: `GATED_DELTA_NET` is **1.6%** of a prefill graph, the whole DeltaNet core 2.7%, full attention plus the QSA indexer 1.5%. Nor is it host overhead — **93% of the wall clock is GPU kernel time**. It is MoE experts 35.7%, dense matmul 26.2%, **elementwise glue 30.6%** and **tiny-N F32 matmul 12.2%**, of which `hc_*_inject` — a `[10240, 4]` F32 projection run 95 times a graph — is **10.3% of prefill at 31.8 GFLOP/s** and fuses into `hc.down` for free. Against this repo's own measured kernels the chunk is **2.25x on matmul** and **2.53x on the experts** (§2.2's Q4 grouped block), so **~1150 tok/s, not ~2000, is what L6 should be scoped against**. Two more: **`-ub 512` is a MALL-sized optimum** — 256/512/1024/2048 give 347.7/**391.4**/380.9/336.7, because the 10240-wide F32 residual is 20.97 MB at T=512 and 83.9 MB at T=2048, and the glue costs 1.57x more per token when it stops fitting; and at **decode** the matmuls are already at 198-230 GB/s, so the whole 25.15 -> 38.2 gap is **2896 weightless dispatches costing 8.9 ms, 22% of the step** — an order of magnitude past L1's 0.62 ms estimate |

# research/ — the findings archive

One file per **completed** experiment, plus (since the 2026-09-20
consolidation) the frozen per-vertical progress files. The live state of
play and the open items are in [`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md); this directory
is where a finished item's full write-up lives once it is closed, so an
agent can load one finding without loading all of them. The phase-1
backlog and the measured roofline are archived in [`ideas.md`](ideas.md).

## The vertical archives

The root progress files were consolidated here on 2026-09-20, frozen as
each vertical's closing record; stage letters (L7d, P4c, T9, S10, I7, E7…)
resolve inside them.

**`IMAGE.md` named two different files**, so a citation of it needs one
extra step: with a **Q-stage, a numbered decision or a Q-o number** it is

from 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-21); with an **I-stage (I0–I7)** it is

name: moe-gemm-screening
description: "How to screen a build of the LLM's grouped MoE GEMM (llm_moe_gemm.comp) from disk, and the three traps hit doing it (2026-09-29/30)."

`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are
`moeSPIRV`'s keys in `llm/gpu_moe.go`; the auto plan is m2 at ≤256 tokens and
m4 above (moved from 1024 by §2.12), so a 2048-token screen must override
`up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build (WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one. The
shared expert runs the **Q8_0** builds of the same rungs (`up_q80_m4`,
`down_q80_m4`), so a screen that changes the schedule must load those too.

**Why:** three traps cost time (KERNELS.md G5a/G5c, research/2.11, 2.12).
The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. A `-moe` arm at
60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean. And
since §2.12 the permutation aligns experts to **16 rows**, and every
single-wave build is a `SHORT` build that bounds its tiles by the record's
real rows: a build compiled **without** `-DSHORT=1` loaded through
`LLM_MOE_SPV` writes the next expert's rows unless `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` is set
(it is what the pre-§2.12 controls need). A SHORT build that rounds its tile
count up (`SHORT_STEP=2`) must still bound the *store* by the real count; the
first cut stored the rounded tiles and `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` caught it as
"every plan with m4 in the up position disagrees".

**How to apply:** build arms with glslc to the scratchpad (the generate line's
flags from `shaders/shaders.go` plus the knob), `cmp` the knob-less build
against the shipped `.spv` (ids may differ; compare `cmd/probe` instruction
counts), gate with `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (maxAbs must be 0 against m2/m2)
and `TestMoEGPUPaddingIsInert`, then time; the whole-model identity is
`TestGraphLogits`'s diagnostics reproduced to the digit against an old test
binary built in a `git worktree` (symlink `models/` and `reference/out/`,
copy `shaders/*.spv`). A control that removes work can read above the pipe's
ceiling only if the compiler dropped MMAs; check the `v_wmma` count in the
disassembly before trusting it. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and
[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].

`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are

m4 above, so a 2048-token screen must override `up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build
(WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one.

**Why:** two traps cost time on 2026-09-29 (KERNELS.md G5a, research/2.11).
The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. And a `-moe` arm
at 60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean.

**How to apply:** build arms with glslc to the scratchpad (the generate line's
flags from `shaders/shaders.go` plus the knob), `cmp` the knob-less build
against the shipped `.spv` (ids may differ; compare `cmd/probe` instruction
counts), gate with `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (maxAbs must be 0 against m2/m2),
then time. A control that removes work can read above the pipe's ceiling only
if the compiler dropped MMAs; check the `v_wmma` count in the disassembly

[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].

[← IDEAS.md](ideas.md) · [research index](README.md) · the grouped MoE GEMM's padding

### 2.12 The grouped MoE GEMM's short last tile: the alignment one fragment, the loop one of WM copies — **done** ✅ (2026-09-30)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G5, after §2.11): the up projection's executed
rate at 2048 tokens is 37 TFLOP/s of a ~49 ceiling, and on top of it sits
a **1.90x padding factor**: the permutation rounds every expert's row
range up to the widest row block in the plan (64), so 608 tiles execute
38 912 rows for 20 480 real ones. P11-4 tried three ways of padding to the
fragment instead and every one was a wash or a loss, because *then* the
kernel was bound by its slab unpack and the rows were nearly free. §2.11's
pipeline made the MMAs ~78% of the kernel. Are the rows the cost now?

**Answer: yes, and the down projection's more than the up's.** The
alignment is now sixteen rows, the permutation's record already said how
many of a block's rows are real, and the single-wave builds of
`llm_moe_gemm.comp` are `SHORT` builds that run one of WM copies of their
K loop and store chosen by a uniform switch on that count — no bound inside
the unrolled loops, the same MMAs per real row in the same order, so it is
**bit-identical** to the padded schedule (`TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` at
`maxAbs == 0` across every mixed plan, `TestGraphLogits`'s whole-model
diagnostics reproduced to the digit against the old build). At 2048
tokens `moe.up` **6 994 / 7 029 → 6 314 / 6 255 µs a layer (1.11x)**,
`moe.down` **6 577 / 6 609 → 5 370 / 5 339 (1.23x)** on the checkpoint's
Q5_1 and **5 373 → 4 209 (1.28x)** on the served IQ4_NL, the block
**1.13–1.14x**; whole-model prefill **1 417 / 1 419 → 1 514 / 1 513 tok/s
at 2048 (1.07x)**, 1 500 / 1 502 → 1 549 / 1 543 at 4096, 1 461 / 1 467 →
1 481 / 1 483 at 8192. And with the padding no longer a price on the wide
rung, the plan's m2/m4 boundary moves from 1024 tokens to 256.

**What the padding was.** `Schedule()` on the 4k trace's real routing,
executed rows over real (the tile count is the same at both alignments,
because an expert's last block is still a block):

| tokens | rows | pad 64 (was) | pad 16 | pad 32 (what the up m4 build executes) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 5 120 | 11 904 (2.33x) | 8 064 (1.57x) | 11 904 at the m2 rung's own 32 |
| 1024 | 10 240 | 17 536 (1.71x, m2) | 13 472 (1.32x) | 17 536 |
| 2048 | 20 480 | 38 912 (1.90x) | 24 304 (1.19x) | 28 832 (1.41x) |
| 4096 | 40 960 | 59 904 (1.46x) | 44 816 (1.09x) | 49 536 (1.21x) |

**The arm.** The record's third word has carried the block's real rows
since C5 (the decode GEMV skips its padding with it); the GEMM never read
it. A SHORT build rounds it up to the schedule's alignment (`pc.gemmM`,
`MoEGPU.pad`, so a plan that mixes in a multi-wave rung and aligns to 64
still runs whole blocks) and takes `wmEff = ceil(rows / 16)`; the K loop
and the epilogue are macros over the tile count and the kernel holds one
instantiation per height behind `switch (wmEff)`. The pipeline's first
fetch, the permutation entries and the accumulators' zeroing sit before
the switch and are shared. MODE 0's A staging still fills all 64 rows —
the loads are in flight behind the MMAs, and the rows past the block are
valid entries of the permuted space (the permutation sentinel-fills to a
whole 64-row block past its end, which `maxRows` has room for) — so only
the MMAs and the stores of the missing tiles go. `llm_moe_perm.comp` cuts
`ceil(padded / bm)` records an expert instead of `padded / bm`; the
host's `pad()` is the max over the plan's rungs of `moeAlign` (16 for a
single-wave rung or a GEMV, the block for `w2m1`/`w4m1`), `maxTiles` has a
pad-below-block form, the tile arenas are sized for the widest alignment
whatever the plan, and the shared expert's host-written list gets a short
last block the same way. `LLM_MOE_PAD=16|32|64` forces the alignment for a
screen.

**The register and code line** (`cmd/probe`, `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats`,
wave64), which decided the form the up build ships in:

| build | copies | VGPRs | spilled | instructions | code |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `up_q4k_m4` shipped (§2.11) | — | 256 | 0 | 1 544 | 8.6 KB |
| SHORT, every height | 1, 2, 3, 4 | 256 | **15** | 4 524 | 25.6 KB |
| SHORT without the 3-tile copy | 1, 2, 4 | 256 | **15** | 3 339 | 18.9 KB |
| SHORT without the 1-tile copy | 2, 3, 4 | 256 | **15** | 3 753 | 21.2 KB |
| **SHORT, `SHORT_STEP=2` (shipped)** | **2, 4** | 256 | **0** | 2 504 | 14.1 KB |
| `up_q4k_m2` SHORT | 1, 2 | 240 | 0 | 1 732 | |
| `up_q5k_m4` / `up_q80_m4` SHORT (plain loop) | 1–4 | 256 | 0 | 5 979 / 4 811 | |

and the first cut that stored the rounded tiles was a race the ladder test

Root `KERNELS.md` (opened 2026-09-29, G-stages) is the live plan for taking the WMMA kernels from 42.0 toward 55.5 TFLOP/s. Facts a session needs before touching it: the suite's best GEMM ran at 2813 MHz / 137 W where the `peak` probe ran 2899 / 110, so utilisation is quoted per clock (478 FLOP/clk/CU is the measured peak); the shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8` is 240 VGPRs, no spill, `BK_TILES 1`, no prefetch; both head-128 attentions spill 112–126 VGPRs. `cmd/probe` (RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats/asm) was deleted by accident on 2026-09-22 and restored 2026-09-29.

G0/G1 (2026-09-29, research §0.6, §6.5): **no real kernel runs at 2899 MHz.** A video forward runs at 2600–2650 MHz and ~149 W (package-limited ~150 W), so its ceiling is 49.9 TFLOP/s, not 55.5; a 20 ms bench burst sees 2813. **32 busy CPU threads halve the GPU clock** and make a forward 1.67x slower: never run a CPU-heavy job (staging, audio decode, a test sweep) beside a device timing, and sample `hwmon/freq1_input` + `power1_average` around any in-pipeline number. The shipped GEMM's rate is flat from 1 to 3+ workgroups a CU, and ACO does not prefetch across K tiles.

G2 (2026-09-29, research §2.9): the GEMM ships as `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (+ `_krange`) for H3: K slabs staged through LDS at wave32, 4x4 tiles, eight waves, bit-identical, 74 → 80% per clock, a 480p forward 29.9 → 27.1 s. G8 (same day) carried it to all nine hosts through their own gates: image step 2179 → 2058 ms, VAE decode 37.1 → 35.5 s, Kev fp16 at 494 tokens 154 → 132 ms; it loses below ~1000 rows ([[lds-gemm-needs-a-full-machine]]). The mechanism and what it rules out: [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]]; the screen: [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

G5 (2026-09-29, research §2.11): started as "Q4 B fragments built in registers" and measured out of it before it was built. On the LLM's MoE up GEMM (`llm_moe_gemm.comp`) the LDS round trip is ~8 points and the loop without its stagings already runs at the pipe; the cost was the dependent, divergent bank-load chain in front of every K-step, each block's lines re-read 2–8x. The K loop as a software pipeline with each block's bytes fetched once (`-DPIPE=2`) is bit-identical, `moe.up` 1.68x at 2048 tokens, whole-model prefill 1194 → 1407 tok/s. The same pipeline on the down mode moves Q5_1 by nothing and IQ4_NL by 1.05x (shipped for IQ4_NL only). Lesson: price a kernel's parts by their absence (`MOE_*` knobs, `LLM_MOE_SPV`, [[moe-gemm-screening]]) before building the arm the plan names; a two-set (ping-pong) register pipeline spilled and lost, the one-set form won.

**Why:** eight verticals ended on "the GEMMs are at their ceiling" without the ceiling ever being pushed; a GEMM win lands in every served request.

**How to apply:** file a closed finding under the next free `§N.M` in `research/` and point the G-stage at it; prove a lever in `gemm_wmma.comp`'s suite first, ship it in `dit_gemm.comp`, and screen it with each vertical's own tool ([[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]]).

Done. G5c is built, gated, measured and recorded. Nothing is committed: the auto-committer owns main.

**What the item was.** After G5a the MoE up GEMM's largest remaining term was its padding: the permutation rounded every expert's rows to the widest row block (64), so at 2048 tokens 608 tiles executed 1.90x the rows that exist. P11 had tried a short last tile and found it a wash because the slab unpack was the cost then; §2.11 made the MMAs ~78% of the kernel, so the rows were worth re-pricing.

**What shipped.** The permutation now aligns experts to one fragment (16 rows). Every single-wave build of the grouped GEMM is a `SHORT` build: the record's real-row count picks one of WM copies of the K loop and store through a uniform switch, so there is no bound inside the unrolled loops and the MMAs per real row are the same in the same order. The Q4_K up m4 build keeps only its 2- and 4-tile copies, because any third copy spills 15 registers and a control with the alignment forced back to 64 priced that at 9% on full blocks. The plan's m2/m4 boundary moved from 1024 tokens to 256 on the new ladder.

**Gates.** The ladder test agrees to the bit across every mixed plan, the padding-inertness test passes, all 56 MoE, chunk-split and attention tests pass, and `TestGraphLogits` on the new build prints the same whole-model diagnostics to the digit as an old-tree build.

**Numbers at 2048 tokens, old vs new, two interleaved runs (µs a layer):**

| kernel | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| moe.up | 6994 / 7029 | 6314 / 6255 (1.11x) |
| moe.down, Q5_1 | 6577 / 6609 | 5370 / 5339 (1.23x) |
| moe.down, served IQ4_NL | 5373 | 4209 (1.28x) |
| block, IQ4_NL | 14441 | 12727 |

Whole-model prefill, same-hour A/B twice: 1417/1419 → 1514/1513 tok/s at 2048 (1.07x), 1500/1502 → 1549/1543 at 4096, 1461/1467 → 1481/1483 at 8192.

**One bug on the way, worth knowing.** The first two-copy cut stored the rounded-up tile over the next expert's rows, a race the ladder test caught as "every plan with m4 in the up position disagrees". The store is now bounded by the real count; the memory note on MoE screening records it, along with the new trap that a pre-§2.12 build loaded through `LLM_MOE_SPV` needs `LLM_MOE_PAD=64`.

**Records.** `research/2.12-moe-short-tiles.md` has the full ladder, the register table and the row-cost analysis; KERNELS.md carries the G5 row, a G5c section, the handoff and the how-to-run knob; the research index and TODO.md's prefill line are updated; four CSVs are in `results/g5c_moe_short_*`.

**What the analysis points at next.** A short tile's rows are cheap rows (0.086 µs against 0.137) because the tile still unpacks two whole slabs, about 300 VALU instructions a lane a step at a matrix clock each. That unpack is now the largest term in the up projection at every rung, so G5's `v_perm`/`v_cvt_pk` idea is the next lever on this kernel, then the Q5_K up build and the down mode's A fragment loads, or G4 (attention) as the plan's order says. The served binary still needs a redeploy to pick this up.
